nate: Heads-up — rolling numbers from the canary show a clear p99 regression on llama3-13b after the rope_theta tweak. Hoping to triage quickly, looks related to kernel selection + KV cache saturation.

aj: saw the alert, thanks. which kernel path is winning on those requests?

nate: kernel selector moved traffic to fused-l2l3 path at ~60% of requests for chattemplate longer sessions. The weird bit is we see head-split events (one head group stuck on slow path) and kv cache churn.

maria: can you paste the perf snapshot?

nate: paste from perf-bot: ```
profile: run=canary-2026-03-17 model=llama3-13b
p50=28ms p95=72ms p99=210ms (baseline p99=98ms)
kernel-path-distribution: fused-l2l3=61%, l1fused=27%, fallback=12%
kv-cache-evictions/s=0.44 (baseline 0.02)
head-split-count=34 over 10m window
```

perf-bot: pmr link: https://perf.redwood/canary/3976543210 (summary + flamegraphs) :zap:

aj: kv-cache-evictions jumping that much will blow tail latency. Any change in prefix length distribution on the canary traffic?

nate: yes — we enabled chat_template padding for a subset of sessions, average prefix tokens up from 64 -> 180. That increased KV sizes and exposed a hot-kv slot that triggers async eviction more frequently.

sam: did the kernel selector account for typical KV working set size before routing to fused-l2l3? I thought fused path assumes stable small kv cache.

maria: it does heuristically, but selector currently uses a simple static threshold: if seq_len <= 512 and avg_kv_entries < 256 -> fused-l2l3. With padding, avg_kv_entries calculation is stale.

aj: so selector misrouted heavy sessions to a kernel optimized for small KV -> heavy mem thrash -> fallback slow path and head-split.

nate: exactly. Repro gist (local): ```python
# quick repro: create requests with chatpad padding 180 tokens
for i in range(1000):
  req = make_request(model='llama3-13b', prefix_tokens=180, stream=False)
  send(req)
```
Results: continuous tail spikes, evictions rise.

maria: quick mitigation options? 1) revert rope_theta tweak, 2) force selector to avoid fused-l2l3 for sessions with padding>128, 3) tweak kv eviction threshold.

sam: I prefer 2 + 3 as short-term — revert would be heavy. Can we flip a runtime flag?

aj: yes we have selector override flags per model tag. I can push a canary config to mark chat-template-padding as "avoid-fused".

perf-bot: running quick smoke with override... ETA ~4m.

nate: thanks. Longer term we should make selector consider measured live KV working set quantiles (p75/p95) not just averages. Also prefer conservative fused routing when head-dim mismatch or siLU/RMSNorm variants present — those change kernel perf characteristics.

maria: agree. Also add a small hysteresis window so short bursts of long prefixes don't flip routing too fast. Maybe maintain per-session rolling window of kv_entries and only route when stable for N requests.

aj: I'll draft a small change: selector checks p75_kv_entries < 200 AND not chatpad-padded -> fused. Otherwise route to l1fused. Push as config flag first.

sam: logging ask: add a counter for head-split incidents per kernel decision so we can correlate future regressions to the selector choice.

nate: also let's capture kernel-level mem stats in flamegraphs (peak KV bytes) to diagnose quantization interactions. Quick note — quantized kernels (4/8-bit) show slightly different eviction patterns because buffer packing varies. Worth measuring after canary.

perf-bot: smoke results: override applied -> p99 down from 210ms -> 95ms, kv-evictions/s -> 0.03. No head-splits observed in 10m window.

maria: nice. aj, can you ship the override to prod as a staged rollout? Start with 10% -> 50% -> 100% if stable. Add the logging metrics sam asked for.

aj: will do. Creating rollout ticket and feature flag.

sam: I'll add the p75/p95 metric hooks to selector, and a small README on why fused routing needs kv stability.

nate: TL;DR: regression was not purely rope_theta; it was an interaction between chat padding (larger KV), stale avg-based kernel selector, and fused kernel assumptions. Hotfix is selector override + better eviction thresholds; long-term is quantile-aware selection + hysteresis + kernel mem metrics.

maria: ack. Good postmortem once prod is stable. :thumbsup:
